en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Subduing Poisonous Harm by the Kanyā Khaṇḍarohī, an Emanation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. [Composed by] Su Guo,
Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Special Advancement.

The Imperial Preceptor, who held a fief of three thousand households, was invested with the purple robe and posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works; his posthumous name was Dajian (Great Mirror), and his honorific title was Dayangzhi (Great Universal Wisdom). Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery, by imperial decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in the Jeta Grove at Śrāvastī together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by countless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and the eight classes of beings, all of whom had gathered like clouds. At that time,
the Tathāgata addressed the great assembly.
I recall that in the past,
while dwelling north of the Snowy Mountains and traveling to Mount Gandhamādana,
I saw a young girl.
His body was adorned with the marks and secondary signs of a hundred merits;
he wore a deer skin as a garment and used various venomous snakes as a necklace.
Various venomous insects, tigers, wolves,
and lions constantly surrounded him as his companions;
he drank the juice of poisonous fruits and ate the fruit of poisonous herbs.
Seeing me, she spoke these words:
"Virtuous one, listen as I proclaim a single great mantra capable of eliminating all poisons in the world."
If anyone hears this mantra and recollects my name,
they shall not be harmed by any poisons whatsoever.
At that time, the young girl spoke the mantra for me.
Having heard this,
I shall always maintain this mantra to benefit sentient beings.
I shall now recite the mantra, which says:

*Tadyathā | oṃ irimeḍi trimedī irimeḍi irimeḍi nūme numariye ṇuṃce ṇuṃcarie dakaṇi vajraṇi ghasmiṇi ghasmiramukte agha aghani aghanaghana ghani iriye iririye akhyaye upakhaye śvete śvetadundubhe ānānurākṣasi svāhā.* The Buddha said: "O bhikṣus..."
If a person hears this dhāraṇī even once,
after seven years they will be free from all poisons;
if a person constantly recollects it, [the same shall hold].
No venomous insects or any poisonous drugs whatsoever shall be able to harm them.
Should any venomous snake come to bite such a person,
that snake will immediately rot away.
For anyone who receives and maintains this dhāraṇī rite,
they must first make offerings of white substances to their teacher;
thereafter, upon receiving [the transmission], the rite will certainly be accomplished.
Do not recite this mantra near a snake;
the snake will die immediately. Once it has died, one shall cause it to revive by reciting the following mantra:

*tadyathā | iri miri garami ca kṣakulu kṣakulu kṣakuluna kṣakuluna garamine kuta kuta ye te saputa saputa ye te nāgale nāgañcaka laṇḍiri icce ra buśa śidra beḍra siputa siputa svāhā*. If a person recites this once, [the snake shall be restored].
Throughout the year, one will not be afflicted by external poisons.
If one can constantly maintain this, external poisons will be extinguished,
and the three internal poisons will likewise be eliminated.
If one suffers from malignant sores, carbuncles on the back, swellings, or similar ailments,
by spitting upon them while reciting the mantra, they will be immediately cured.
Even if all manner of malevolent beasts should approach, [the same applies].
If one merely recites it seven times, it will pass away and cannot cause harm.
If one has been poisoned,
place [the mantra] upon the first joint at the tip of the middle finger.
Circumambulate the sore with the left and right hands, reciting the mantra twenty-one times while turning against the direction of the sun; it will then be cured.
One must always recite it quietly and not in a loud voice.
If the sound is loud, poisonous insects will surely die.
Once the evil insects have died,
if one releases them with this mantra, they will immediately come back to life.
Recite this twenty-one times.
The mantra for neutralizing poison is as follows:
*tadyathā* | *iḷe mili pili nāgacchagalanti iṭṭhe raṃśa kīṭṭha sīṭṭha ḍaṃṭṭha sīṭṭha sarvaha*. If a person suffers from carbuncles on the back...
If one turns it in the opposite direction and writes it upside down in a single circuit, [the ailment] will be cured immediately;
the evil substance will emerge of its own accord, and there is great spiritual efficacy.
After the Buddha had spoken these words, [he continued].
The Great Assembly rejoiced and rose at that time.
The *Rāguliye-kumārikā-viṣa-damana-mantra-sūtra*.
